raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Default MiniMax-M3 (`MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM`, `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`) to breakable CUDA graphs on ROCm, as DeepSeek-V4.1 and HY4 (#64763) already are. Draft until the accuracy checks below are done.

## Claims

- On ROCm, steps whose prefill + decode rows fit the prefill capture size (512 tokens by default) replay piecewise graphs, with the sparse attention running eagerly between the pieces, instead of running the whole step eagerly; decode steps keep their full graphs.
- MI355X TP4: a 64-512-token prompt alone reaches its first token 58-75% sooner; next to 2 running decodes, a 64-384-token prompt 42-52% sooner. Prompts above the capture size are unchanged.
- InferenceX AgentX on the same setup with the prefill capture cap raised to 2048 (first 20 min, one run per side): c16 TTFT p50 -15.5% and interactivity p90 +5.7%; c32 within noise (+1-2% interactivity).
- Cost: 6.1 GiB more graph memory per rank (~2 MiB per captured HIP graph on ROCm, see Details), 3.4% fewer KV cache tokens, engine init 8 s longer.
- `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` restores today's behavior.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k breakable` and pre-commit in a ROCm container on MI355X: 37 passed.
- MI355X TP4, `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c`, the InferenceX AgentX c16 serve command (7 speculative tokens with synthetic acceptance 4.04, NVFP4 KV and indexer caches, `--max-num-seqs 32`), with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` vs `=1` (`=1` is what this PR makes the default); one server after the other on the same 4 GPUs. Each point is the p50 of 12 random-token prompts with `max_tokens=1` (time to first token, ms), each prompt fresh so the prefix cache never hits. Alone: mean of two rounds. Next to 2 decodes: 2 requests with 8192-token prompts keep decoding while the prompts arrive.

| prompt tokens | alone: off -> **on** | next to 2 decodes: off -> **on** |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 67.6 -> **16.8** (-75%) | 86.1 -> **41.7** (-52%) |
| 128 | 66.3 -> **19.5** (-71%) | 82.4 -> **45.3** (-45%) |
| 256 | 80.8 -> **23.9** (-70%) | 91.1 -> **50.2** (-45%) |
| 384 | 77.3 -> **28.9** (-63%) | 93.7 -> **54.2** (-42%) |
| 512 | 76.2 -> **32.1** (-58%) | 92.8 -> 93.5 (+1%, 528-token step: eager) |
| 768 | 77.7 -> 78.4 (+1%) | 91.9 -> 90.1 (-2%) |
| 1024 | 77.0 -> 77.1 (0%) | 92.3 -> 90.7 (-2%) |
| 2048 | 80.0 -> 78.1 (-2%) | 97.4 -> 96.8 (-1%) |
| 4096 | 124.3 -> 122.6 (-1%) | 150.5 -> 150.2 (0%) |

- `--cudagraph-metrics` confirms the modes: with breakable graphs every step of at most 512 tokens ran PIECEWISE and larger ones NONE; without them every step with prefill rows ran NONE.
- The decodes sharing those steps also speed up: at 64-128-token prompts their mean chunk interval drops from ~28 ms to 14-15 ms (decode alone: 11.4 ms).
- Startup, from the server logs (per rank): graph capture 7 s / 1.38 GiB -> 16 s / 7.49 GiB; KV cache 13,412,992 -> 12,961,536 tokens (-3.4%); engine init 15.7 -> 23.7 s.
- InferenceX AgentX (the CI client, agentx-harness 1.0.12, and its dataset; the serve command above at c16 / c32 with `--max-num-seqs` 32 / 64), first 20 minutes of each point after the warm-up, one run per side, both sides of a concurrency one after the other on the same 4 GPUs: `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` vs `=1` with `--compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 2048}'`.

  | metric | c16: off -> **breakable, cap 2048** | c32: off -> **breakable, cap 2048** |
  |---|---|---|
  | interactivity p50 / p90 (1000 / ITL) | 211.5 -> **217.2** (+2.7%) / 140.1 -> **148.1** (+5.7%) | 158.1 -> 161.8 (+2.3%) / 92.1 -> 93.2 (+1.2%) |
  | TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 348 -> **294** (-15.5%) / 998 -> 948 (-5.0%) | 377 -> 374 (-0.8%) / 1265 -> 1212 (-4.2%) |
  | ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | 4.73 -> 4.61 / 7.14 -> 6.75 | 6.32 -> 6.18 / 10.85 -> 10.73 |
  | E2E latency per output token p50 / p90 (ms) | 6.16 -> 5.87 / 10.63 -> 10.05 | 8.10 -> 7.98 / 15.40 -> 15.25 |
  | output tok/s per GPU | 150.1 -> 150.3 | 346.0 -> 345.7 |
  | completed requests | 674 -> 677 | 1820 -> 1830 |
  | prefill or mixed steps in piecewise graphs (`--cudagraph-metrics`) | 0 of 683 -> 381 of 687 (55%) | 0 of 1749 -> 989 of 1764 (56%) |
  | KV cache tokens / graph memory per rank | 13.41M / 1.38 GiB -> 12.07M / 19.30 GiB | 13.37M / 1.79 GiB -> 12.01M / 19.69 GiB |

  c32 moves within run-to-run noise (~2%); the c16 TTFT and p90 gains need a second run. AgentX was not run at this PR's default cap (512).
- Pending: gsm8k with real speculative decoding and single short requests at concurrency 1 with breakable graphs on.

## Details

Why: M3 cannot `torch.compile` on ROCm, so the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` falls back to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` ("the loaded model provides neither a compiled submodule nor breakable CUDA graphs"), and every step that carries prefill rows runs eagerly. An eager step of up to ~1K tokens costs 65-80 ms regardless of its size (launch-bound); the piecewise replay costs 17-32 ms. The AMD model already marks its sparse attention as the break (`@eager_break_during_capture` on `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._run_attention`). Short prefills are common in agentic serving: in a 15-minute InferenceX AgentX c16 run on the nightly image, 55% of the prefill or mixed steps carried at most 2048 tokens and 18% at most 512 (566 such steps, 1.2% of all steps).

Tradeoffs / limitations:
- Only steps up to `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` (default 512 on ROCm) benefit. Raising it is left to the deployment. The same setup with the cap at 2048 (`max_cudagraph_capture_size` on that image: 147 sizes instead of 51), one round each on the same 4 GPUs, TTFT p50 ms:

  | prompt tokens | alone: cap 512 -> **2048** | next to 2 decodes: cap 512 -> **2048** |
  |---|---|---|
  | 64-256 | equal | equal (+1-2%) |
  | 512 | 32.0 -> 32.0 | 91.9 -> **58.8** (-36%) |
  | 768 | 78.6 -> **40.1** (-49%) | 90.4 -> **67.7** (-25%) |
  | 1024 | 79.3 -> **47.8** (-40%) | 92.8 -> **71.3** (-23%) |
  | 1536 | 79.7 -> **57.5** (-28%) | 91.9 -> 86.5 (-6%) |
  | 2000 | 83.3 -> **68.5** (-18%) | 94.6 -> 94.2 (0%) |
  | 2048 | 80.8 -> **68.5** (-15%) | 97.6 -> 98.4 (a 2064-token step: eager) |
  | 3072 / 4096 | equal | equal |

  Cost per rank: graph memory 7.49 -> 19.30 GiB, KV cache 12.96M -> 12.07M tokens (-6.9%), capture 21 -> 32 s. The cost grows linearly with the number of capture sizes, ~123 MiB each: a breakable capture of this model is 61 HIP graphs (60 attention breaks), and every HIP graph currently holds ~2 MiB of VRAM for its kernel-argument pool (ROCm/rocm-systems#15012, fix proposed in ROCm/rocm-systems#14794). The gain per size shrinks as steps grow: next to decodes it is gone by ~1.5-2K tokens.
- The mono decode path (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO=1`) only runs under decode-only graphs; it now needs `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` or `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` (documented in the new `docs/models/minimax_m3.md`).
- Not a duplicate: #56075 only enables breakable graphs in the AMD disaggregated CI config; #63070 does the same default change for GLM-5.3-Flash.

---

@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+# MiniMax-M3
+
+vLLM supports MiniMax-M3 (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, etc.)
+through `MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM` and `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`.
+
+## AMD ROCm graph execution
+
+MiniMax-M3 on AMD ROCm uses breakable HIP graphs by default, without `torch.compile`.
+Decode steps replay full graphs. Steps with prefill rows, up to
+`max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` tokens, replay piecewise graphs with the sparse
+attention running eagerly between the pieces; without them every such step runs eagerly.
+Set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` to go back to decode-only graphs.
+
+The mono decode path (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO=1`) serves decode steps under
+decode-only graphs only: pass `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`
+or `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` with it.
+
+See [CUDA graphs](../design/cuda_graphs.md) for graph execution modes; the same
+configuration terminology applies to HIP graphs on ROCm.

     if current_platform.is_cuda():
